To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a recursive construction is the most natural way to design a convolutional circuit, that the area–time tradeoff is the most important design criterion, and that a family of convolutional circuits can be designed that are all optimal with respect to this criterion.
a recursive architecture is a good choice for a convolutional circuit, and that it is possible to construct an optimal circuit for convolution by using a recursive architecture.
the area–time optimal convolver is a 3–stage circuit with a 3–bit adder and a 2–stage pipeline.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problems.
the design of VLSI convolution circuits that are optimal with respect the area–time tradeoff.
the design and analysis of VLSI architectures for convolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the recursive construction is a very powerful tool to design VLSI convolution circuits.
the area–time product of a VLSI convolution circuit is a linear function of the convolution degree.
the area–time optimal VLSI circuit for open polynomial multiplication is the recursive circuit with a degree of pipeline equal to the degree of the polynomials to be multiplied.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found the optimal tradeoff for a wide variety of VLSI convolvers.
, for any given area, the best circuit can be found among the family.
we present a complete family of optimal circuits for polynomial multiplication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the area–time optimal convolver is not a trivial circuit.
a large number of different circuits can be obtained with a single design.
the recursive approach is a powerful tool to design optimal circuits for polynomial multiplication.
